title: A Twice-a-Year Shot to Prevent HIV
hook: South Africa is rolling out lenacapavir — an HIV-prevention injection given just twice a year — a potential game-changer for a country at the center of the epidemic, if doses and funding hold up.
key_points: Lenacapavir is a long-acting injectable for HIV prevention (PrEP), given only twice a year.
Twice-yearly dosing sidesteps the hard part of daily prevention pills: remembering them every day.
South Africa, one of the hardest-hit countries, is rolling it out as a major prevention tool.
U.S. aid cuts and limited dose supply threaten to slow how widely it reaches people.
As distribution widens beyond South Africa, early reviews are mixed on whether doses reach the places that need them most.
content_html: HIV prevention has long leaned on a daily pill — effective, but only if you actually take it every day. South Africa, one of the countries hit hardest by the epidemic, is now rolling out an alternative that could change the math: lenacapavir, a long-acting injection that prevents HIV with just two doses a year.
extra_html:
The promise, as NPR reports, is adherence. "Take it every day" is a real barrier for many people, whether because of stigma, access, or simply life getting in the way. A shot you get twice a year turns prevention into something closer to a routine checkup — far easier to sustain across a population.

The catch is supply and money. Cuts to U.S. foreign aid and a limited number of available doses threaten to blunt the rollout's reach, meaning the people who could benefit most may not all get access soon. It's a striking example of how a scientific breakthrough and the systems that deliver it are two different problems — and both have to work for the impact to be real.

Update (August 2026): NPR revisited the rollout as distribution spread to other countries, including Uganda, and found mixed reviews. The drug's effectiveness isn't in question; the debate is about allocation — whether the limited doses are reaching the communities and regions with the greatest need. That gap between "a tool that works" and "a tool that gets to people" is the recurring story of global health.

related.hook: Sexually transmitted infections are common and often symptomless — which is exactly why prevention and testing, not just treatment, are what keep you and your partners healthy.

flashcards.prompt: What makes lenacapavir a potential 'game-changer' for HIV prevention?
flashcards.back_html: It's a long-acting injection given only twice a year. That removes the biggest practical hurdle of daily prevention pills — taking one every single day — which can make protection far easier to keep up.

flashcards.prompt: What threatens to slow South Africa's rollout of the twice-yearly HIV shot?

choices.text: U.S. aid cuts and a limited supply of doses
The drug being unsafe in trials
A lack of anyone at risk of HIV

flashcards.explanation_html: The prevention tool itself is promising; the obstacles described are funding shortfalls from U.S. aid cuts and a limited number of available doses.
